![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059223/assets/ab10c9d133e6a383439b0a8b89643564f5f438d061dba647288927102e870a1b.png)

The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-1$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=2.$

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=-3$ and $x=1.$*

${f}^{′}(-1)≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=-1$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{f(-1+2)-f(-1-2)}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{f(1)-f(-3)}{4} \\  & =\frac{-2-2}{4} \\  & =\frac{(-4)}{4} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
